metric.purpose: Large mono card numbers; the biggest element on a screen.

readout.purpose: Inline mono data: IDs, scores, dates, legend counts.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked muted labels and table headers.

shadows.name: card-rest

narrative.overview: This dashboard reads like a calibrated readout, not a website. The numbers lead and everything else gets out of their way. A dark slate shell frames bright white data surfaces; monospaced numerals give every count, score, and ID the feel of a gauge you can trust. Color is never decoration - green, amber, and red carry operational meaning and nothing else. Blue is held in reserve for interaction so it can never be mistaken for data. The system is calm by default and loud only where it must be; density is a feature, since operations staff scan many rows fast.
keyCharacteristics: Mono numerals for all data readouts; sans for everything else.
Semantic green / amber / red only; blue only for interaction.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, one soft shadow at most.
Dark shell, bright content - a control surface, not a brochure.

rules.name: The Two-Channel Color Rule
rules.body: Green / amber / red mean data state. Blue means interaction. The two channels never cross.

rules.name: The Quiet-Chrome Rule
rules.body: The slate shell and neutrals fill ~90% of every screen. A state color earns its place only by attaching to a real signal.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Data Rule
rules.body: Any number a user reads as a value is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures; language is always IBM Plex Sans.

rules.name: The Muted-Label Rule
rules.body: Labels and column headers are small, uppercase, tracked, and muted (slate-400).

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A surface is flat at rest with a hairline border. Shadow is a whisper on cards, a step stronger only as hover feedback. A 16px+ blur is wrong here.

dos: Do set every data value in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures; keep IBM Plex Sans for all language.
Do use green / amber / red only to signal real state, and keep blue for interaction only.
Do keep surfaces flat: white fill, 1px slate-200 border, at most shadow-sm.
Do pair every color signal with a text label so meaning survives for color-blind users (WCAG 2.1 AA).
Do keep labels and table headers small, uppercase, tracked, and muted (slate-400).
Do show a muted dash for missing data, never a blank cell.
donts: Don't ship consumer-SaaS marketing patterns: no gradients, hero-metric template, glassmorphism, or decorative illustration.
Don't drift toward a generic admin template: no identical icon-card grids, no heavy drop shadows.
Don't recreate the cluttered legacy-enterprise look: keep hierarchy sharp even when the table is dense.
Don't use blue for any data value, and don't use green / amber / red for focus, hover, or selection.
Don't use a shadow blur of 16px or more, or stack shadows for depth.
Don't set body or label text in light gray below 4.5:1 contrast.
